findings.claim:
BT use Theorem 2.3 (Kato 12.4) and Theorem 2.4 (Kato 12.5(1)(2)) only for CM newforms on the way to their unconditional results. Theorem 3.1 is stated for CM f, and it "leads to Theorem 1.1, Theorem 1.2 and Proposition 1.3". Only Remark 3.2, which is conditional, concerns general f.

For CM f, Kato does not prove 12.4 with the §13 Euler-system bound (Thm 13.4) that KatoEulerSystems:L4 plans. He says hypothesis (v) of 13.4 is not satisfied in the CM case. This is certainly true for trivial nebentypus, for example y²=x³−x: every σ in G_{Q(μ_{p∞})} then has a fixed space of dimension 0 or 2. Kato instead proves 12.4(1) in §15.15, using §15.14 when K⊂Q(μ_{p∞}); that is the case K=Q(i), p=2 needed for Theorem 1.2. The proof uses Rubin's elliptic-unit theorem (Kato 15.2), the reciprocity (15.12.2) and the descent (15.13.1). He then gets 12.4(2) by the 13.8 argument, and 12.5(1)(2) by 13.9–13.13, whose construction of z_γ, its independence of choices and the sign relation all use 12.4(2).

No atlas stage plans this CM case:
- L4's text only applies the generic Euler-system bounds "after verifying the representation-theoretic and local hypotheses".
- The accepted Kato decomposition marks §15 as unread, a reading boundary.
- The elliptic-unit main conjecture that the proof needs is itself marked missing in route 7.
- No item states CM H² torsion.

Yet the route 7 brief imports "rational H¹ freeness, H² torsion" for CM forms from KatoEulerSystems L2–L4. As things stand this input is never built. It can be supplied in L4 only by importing the elliptic-unit main conjecture that route 7 builds, and route 7 already lists KatoEulerSystems as a prerequisite, so that would make a KatoEulerSystems ↔ CMAllPrimeMainConjectures cycle. The original report said the plan "would create" a cycle; in fact the cycle arises only if the gap is closed in the planned owner. The CM case therefore belongs in route 7.

Its parenthetical "(not the Galois identification (15.11.2), which Kato says he never uses as such)" gets Kato backwards. findings.claim:
The item cm-newform defines a CM newform as the theta series, or automorphic induction, of an algebraic Hecke character ψ of K with infinity type (1−k,0). That is the conclusion BT §2.2.5 and Kato 15.10 draw from a weaker hypothesis. Kato Remark 12.8, the setting of the §15 argument BT invoke, only asks for an imaginary quadratic K and a continuous Hecke character ψ with L(f,s)=L(ψ,s). The atlas's only other CM predicate is ModularForms Layer 9: a self-twist f = primitive(f⊗χ) with χ≠1.

No stage plans the theorem that links these notions. The theorem: if a weight-k≥2 newform has a nontrivial self-twist χ, or has CM in Kato's sense, then χ=ε_K for an imaginary quadratic K, and f=θ_ψ for an algebraic ψ of type (1−k,0), with the level, nebentypus and conductor dictionary. R17.5 plans only the construction from ψ to f.

The effect is limited. BT's own proofs and applications need only the direction from ψ to f: Theorem 1.1 builds f and f̄ from the character of E/K. The bridge is needed in two places. First, to show that the extraction's definition matches the hypothesis under which Kato §15 and BT Theorems 2.6 and 3.1 are stated. Second, so that these theorems apply to forms the Layer 9 predicate marks as CM, and so that the CM case fits together with Kato's non-CM case (12.8.1–12.8.2).

Theorems 2.6 and 3.1 themselves do not need the direction from f to ψ, and Kato's sense of CM (an identity of L-functions) is a different predicate from the Layer 9 self-twist; the missing theorem is what links them.

The item also misattributes its definition. It says it is 'in Kato's convention' and cites Kato Remark 12.8, but Kato's definition is different. In Remark 12.8, f has CM if L(f,s)=L(ψ,s) for some imaginary quadratic K and some continuous homomorphism ψ: C_K→C^×, where L(ψ,s) runs only over the finite places at which ψ is unramified. Under that definition, the following are consequences that Kato 15.10 asserts without proof: ψ is algebraic of type (1−k,0), its conductor divides N, and F⊂K(ψ(K^×)). BT §2.2.5 repeats the L-function consequence. The equivalence of the two formulations is Kato 15.10 plus strong multiplicity one, which identifies f with the newform induced from ψ. That equivalence is not an item, and no atlas stage plans it. So cm-kato-main and newform-converse, as extracted, are stated only for forms induced from ψ. A newform that has CM in Kato's sense is covered only through this missing equivalence. For k≥2 the two classes are the same, and Theorems 1.1–1.3 are unaffected: BT's proof of Theorem 1.1 takes f and f̄ to be the forms attached to ψ_E and its conjugate.

findings.claim: The item nondescent-density states only the conclusion of Remark 3.6(ii). Its wording, "a positive proportion of twists having analytic rank zero do not descend", leaves open what the proportion is taken over. No item states the counting input the conclusion needs, and the route 8 brief asks for a "counting proof" without saying what is counted. That input is: the twists E^(t) that descend to Q (E^(t) ≅ E'_K for some E'/Q) lie in at most two cosets of the image of Q^×/(Q^×)² in K^×/(K^×)², and they have H-density zero. BT's first sentence can be read two ways. Read as "the rank-zero twists of Proposition 1.3", it is the conclusion itself, asserted without proof. Read as "all twists", a positive proportion of non-descending twists together with a lower density ≥ 1/2 of rank-zero twists gives nothing by inclusion–exclusion. What suffices is that the descending twists have upper density below 1/2. The fact that is true and easy to use is density zero, and it gives a lower density ≥ 1/2 for the twists that have rank zero and do not descend.
findings.evidence:
BT arXiv 2506.03465v2, p.7, Remark 3.6(ii), checked on the page image (v1 is word for word the same): "A positive proportion of the quadratic twists in Proposition 1.3 do not descend to Q. The proposition yields (perhaps) the first examples … the analytic rank being zero for a positive proportion of the quadratic twists of E over F which do not descend to Q." No proof is given. Proposition 1.3 (p.2) and Theorem 3.5 (p.7) say "for at least 50% of t ∈ K^×/(K^×)²". The item's note says only "Keep as a separately proved counting/descent consequence".

Verification:
(1) Since E/K has CM by an order O ⊂ K, K(j(E)) is the ring class field of O. Because j(E) ∈ K, this forces h(O)=1, so j(E) ∈ Q.
(2) Case j ≠ 0,1728. Write E ≅ E_0^(s) with E_0/Q. The quadratic twists over K are classified by K^×/K^×². So E^(t) ≅ E_0^(d) over K, with d ∈ Q^×, if and only if t ∈ s^{-1}·im(Q^×): one coset.
(3) Case j=0. E: y²=x³+B, E^(t): y²=x³+t³B. The twist descends if and only if t³B ∈ Q^×·K^{×6}. Reducing modulo squares, with t³≡t, puts t in the single coset B^{-1}·im Q^×.
(4) Case j=1728. E^(t): y²=x³+t²Ax. The twist descends if and only if t²A = A'u⁴ with A' ∈ Q^×. Here reducing modulo squares gives no constraint (t²≡1), so work modulo fourth powers: (t/u²)² = A'/A, so t ≡ c mod K^×² with c² ∈ A^{-1}Q^×. Any two such c differ by an x with x² ∈ Q^×, that is x ∈ Q^× ∪ √D·Q^×. This gives at most two cosets, and in fact one for K=Q(i), because 2i=(1+i)² gives i≡2.
(5) Heights, with H(t)=∏_{v_𝔭(t) odd}N𝔭 (item number-field-twist-height). For squarefree d ∈ Z, each p|d with p∤disc_K contributes p², whether p is split or inert; ramified p contribute 1. Also H(ct) ≥ H(t)/H(c). So each coset has O(X^{1/2}) classes with H<X.
(6) Classes with H<X correspond to squarefree ideals of norm <X whose class lies in Cl², with fibres of size |O^×/O^×²|·|Cl[2]|. So there are ≍X of them.
So the descending set has density 0. By inclusion–exclusion, the lower density of {rank 0 and not descending} is at least 1/2.

Its title is "Smith's method and the 2-primary class groups of real quadratic fields", and it plans Smith's method as new layers. Its stated scope is 2∞-class groups, not Selmer groups.
